source.title: The Geometry of Saturation: Effective Rank Predicts When Labels Stop Helping in Few-Shot Classification

record.file_problem: Full paper text is present, with minor PDF text-extraction and equation/table-formatting artifacts.
record.tranche_reason: It sweeps training-set size and measures held-out accuracy changes under doubling of the support set, but does not reproduce the original double-descent model-size or epoch experiments.
record.gate_note: The relevant direct outcome is ΔA(K), the change in held-out test accuracy when per-class support size doubles. The paper does not sweep model size or training epochs. Its stop/continue AUC and classification metrics evaluate the diagnostic, not whether test error rises, so they are not separate rows. The paper calls τ = 0.02 a first-to-second-descent boundary, but does not locate an interpolation peak directly.
record.test_reason: The paper evaluates its own stopping diagnostic: how S(K) correlates with, and classifies, marginal accuracy gains on doubling. Double descent is invoked only as theoretical framing (τ = 0.02 as the 'first-to-second descent boundary'). No test-error peak is located. No sign of ΔA near the interpolation point is reported. No result shows more data raising test error. Its results do not bear on whether any version holds.
record.authors_conclusion: Mostly correct. The authors conclude that S(K) predicts diminishing marginal accuracy gains and that τ = 0.02 is a practical label-free stopping rule, a hard stop for PCA-50 and a diminishing-returns monitor for CLIP/DINOv2. The double-descent link (τ marking the first-to-second descent boundary, crossing a peak at K ≈ erank) is asserted theoretically and by citation. It is not demonstrated empirically: no peak or rise in test error is shown.
record.recipe_differences: The study uses few-shot support-size doubling with frozen feature extractors and unregularized logistic regression, rather than the original deep-network model-size, epoch, and data sweeps.
record.method_sensitivity: Reported association varies across backbone/task groups and classifier regularization; PCA-50 binary tasks are more variable, and the measured correlation changes across C values. Saturation threshold outcomes also vary with τ.

fits_no_version.finding: For 9 binary PCA-50 tasks, τ·Ksat at τ = 0.02 approximates estimated erank∞, with a mean ratio of 1.26 (range 1.09–1.42).
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: For linear probes on frozen features, the label budget at which the method's fixed-threshold saturation index is crossed scales with within-class covariance effective rank. This is not a double-descent peak.

record.problems: The paper reports only nine saturated pairs for the τ = 0.02 stop result and gives a wide 95% binomial CI [66%, 100%] for stop-class recall. Its text has internal reporting inconsistencies, including protocol descriptions of 50 trials versus later statements that correlations use seeds 1–5 averaged, and varying pooled effective-rank correlation values across sections/tables. It does not directly identify an interpolation peak.
record.rows_left_out: Stop/continue AUC, precision, recall, and accuracy evaluate the stopping diagnostic rather than the direction of test-error change. The remaining task-level correlations and ablations are not direct measurements of whether adding samples raises test error; the effective-rank saturation-budget results are included as findings outside the listed claim versions.

untested.parts: No reported increase in test error with more samples. The signs of ΔA near the interpolation point (N·K ≈ d) are not reported; meaningful gain is defined on |ΔA|.
No capacity sweep past interpolation across model classes.
Effective rank is related to the method's own threshold budget Ksat, not to a measured peak location on any axis.
No label-noise manipulation and no peak-vs-regularization analysis. The C ablation reports only the correlation ρ.
No re-plotting of risk against an effective parameter count.

missing.what: Sign and size of individual ΔA(K) or A(K) at small K near N·K ≈ d for unregularized logistic regression. This would show whether doubling data lowered accuracy. The paper only bins on |ΔA| and plots ΔA ≥ 0 on the Figure 1 axis.

record.verdict_notes: The paper attributes to Nakkiran et al. the claim that the interpolation peak sits at n ≈ erank(Σ). That is not a result of the original source. Internal inconsistencies appear: 50 trials in the protocol versus seeds 1–5 averaged in §6.13; differing pooled ρ values (0.591 vs 0.6366); and the LR-ablation text says ρ 'decreases' while the numbers increase. The reader's V3 'challenges' label is removed: the 9 saturated pairs lie far past the interpolation point and were selected by the method's own threshold.

versions.untested_parts: No model-size sweep or test-error curve over model size.

The study measures accuracy changes on doubled support sets in few-shot frozen-feature classification, not a full sample-size curve or a directly identified interpolation threshold. It does not report the sign of every individual ΔA.
No capacity sweep across model classes or general risk curves past an interpolation point.
It compares effective rank with a threshold-based support-set saturation budget, not the location of a double-descent peak; it does not test size and epoch axes.

No test of label-noise or variance as the driver of a double-descent peak, multiple peaks, or disappearance under optimally tuned regularization. A classifier-regularization ablation is reported, but it is not a test of those peak claims.
No test of whether counting effective parameters turns a second-descent curve into an ordinary U-shaped curve.

rows.subject: Unregularized logistic regression (C = ∞), aggregate over 49 real tasks and three frozen backbones
rows.operation_detail: Doubled per-class support size and measured the marginal change in held-out accuracy, ΔA(K) = A(2K) − A(K); reported its association with S(K).
rows.measure: Spearman correlation between S(K) and marginal test-accuracy gain ΔA(K)
rows.note: The positive association shows that S(K) tracks marginal gains, but does not establish whether test error rises as sample size increases.
rows.check: A correlation between the method's index S(K) and ΔA is a measure of the diagnostic's performance, not of whether test error rises with more samples. It does not bear on V3.

rows.subject: Unregularized logistic regression (C = ∞), aggregate over saturated doubling pairs
rows.operation_detail: Compared held-out accuracy before and after doubling per-class support size for pairs with S(K) < 0.02.

conditions.value: 9 pairs across the evaluated real-task corpus

rows.measure: Mean marginal test-accuracy change ΔA(K) when support size doubled
rows.note: The reported mean accuracy change is positive rather than a mean increase in test error; the paper does not give the individual signs of all nine changes.
rows.check: These 9 pairs are the method's Stop-triggered subset, a selection on S(K). They sit at K ≥ 1024 on binary PCA-50 tasks, far beyond any interpolation threshold (N·K ≈ d = 50). A small positive mean gain there says nothing about V3, so 'reversed' is wrong. It is own-method evaluation (Table 5), not a V3 result.

relation.reason: Sections 2.5, 7.1 and 7.2 invoke double descent to interpret S(K), but the reported results do not establish a fall-rise-fall risk curve or locate an interpolation peak.

tranche.reason: Uses double descent to motivate its stopping diagnostic and reports diagnostic performance and spectral saturation calibration; it does not measure a double-descent peak or test the claim versions.

source_check.notes: The reported values match the text. Saturation budgets are threshold-defined quantities, not measured double-descent peak locations; the asserted peak-crossing interpretation does not justify verdicts on any claim version.
